chapter: Failure in St. Louis and the Omaha bands
title: St. Louis and Kansas City band scenes compared
summary: He met musicians in St. Louis, names Fate Marable, and says St. Louis bands were polished stock-arrangement outfits while Kansas City had hip nightlife.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I stayed with this family for a short time, I don't know how many -- perhaps a couple of weeks or maybe, you know, for awhile, while I explored the city of St. Louis, which incidently I got a chance to meet the great jazz musicians who were there then, and there were a lot of musicians coming in and out of there, from that town.
Who for instance?
Well, this band -- I can't name all of them now but I -- by name at this moment, but all the great bands that played in the midwest, they either came from St. Louis or Kansas City.
Well, just like Jay McShann.
No, Jay McShann was from Kansas City.
Yes.
And he was also from a later time than this, because Jay McShann is about my age.
Yes.
He was coming up in Kansas City, which
I went to school there later, which I'm going to get to --
And you don't mean Benny Moten, because that was before that.

Benny Moten came from around Kansas City. See, the St. Louis bands were t--they -- I -- you might consider them sort of like a band -- let's see, oh, I can't remember their names now. It's just not clear to me. I can go into the history and speak of it, but if you associate the year that I'm talking about with the band that you find in the history books, you would realize who I'm talking about. Fate Marabel was one of them.
Marable
Yes, yes, I see.

And those bands. Because -- in other words St. Louis -- the two midwestern cities were divided, and St. Louis actually had a different brand of musician than Kansas City. St. Louis had a more organized, polished orchestra type. They played a lot of stock arrangements and that sort of thing, and they had some pretty good singers.
More polished.
Well, no, I wouldn't say more polished, just a different type of music.
I see.
Kansas City had the real hip music, because as you know, Kansas City was quite a town for night life, see.
Yes.
You understand what I mean?
Right.

And St. Louis was more of a town of a little more maybe educational facilities. Incidentally, when I went to Kansas City later I got to know most of the great jazz musicians who I became associated with later in some way, including Count Basie, and Lester Young.
Yes.
